articles.title: Breaking News: Delhi Police Detains Three CJP Leaders Amid Jantar Mantar Protest
articles.description: Delhi Police has detained three CJP leaders—Abhijeet Deep, Ashutosh Raka and Saurabh Das—who reportedly arrived to participate in the protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. According to sources cited in the report, the three leaders were taken to separate locations and had not been released at the time of the broadcast. Security remains tight around Jantar Mantar, where Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in large numbers. Multiple layers of barricades, checkpoints and riot-control vehicles have been positioned along routes leading to the designated protest site. Senior police officers are present on the ground, briefing personnel on maintaining law and order and responding to any attempted gathering. Although security restrictions appear slightly less stringent at some checkpoints compared with the previous day, people are still being questioned about their purpose for entering the area. Access along Ashoka Road is also being monitored. Meanwhile, railway services in the Delhi division have returned to normal following widespread cancellations and disruptions the previous day. According to the report, around 245 trains had been cancelled by 2 PM, including services connected with New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations. Normal operations resumed after midnight, with trains running according to their regular schedules.

articles.title: Protest Alert: CJP Announces Fresh Jantar Mantar March Over SIR
articles.description: The protest over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is set to continue in Delhi, with CJP announcing another demonstration at Jantar Mantar at 10 AM. The organisation has declared that its agitation will continue until Gyanesh Kumar resigns and has appealed to the public to join the protest. Delhi Police has made it clear that permission for the demonstration has not been sought and will not be granted. Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remains in force, with security arrangements similar to those witnessed the previous day. Ground reports from Jantar Mantar indicate that police personnel have been deployed since early morning, with officers receiving briefings and monitoring access to the designated protest site. Although movement around the area appears slightly easier than the previous day, access to the protest location remains restricted. Private vehicles, taxis and auto-rickshaws are being allowed to pass in some areas. At the Delhi–Uttar Pradesh border, police are stopping vehicles, checking passengers and questioning travellers about their destinations. Traffic is moving, but checks are causing queues. Authorities may tighten security further as the announced protest time approaches, with preparations focused on preventing an unauthorised gathering.

articles.title: ‘Undeclared Emergency’: Wangchuk Warns Of Padyatra, Hunger Strike Over Delhi Protest Detentions
articles.description: Social activist Sonam Wangchuk has warned of an indefinite hunger strike or a padyatra if political leaders and activists detained in Delhi are not released by Sunday. Calling the crackdown an “undeclared Emergency”, Wangchuk’s warning follows mass detentions during the Cockroach Janta Party’s protest demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged electoral roll irregularities. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal, TMC chief Mamata Banerjee and several other leaders were detained. Police sources said around 1,500 people had been detained. The INDIA bloc has announced a major protest in Delhi on Monday, October 12, signalling further opposition mobilisation.
